questions.q: What does the summary say arrived in Virginia just before the Pilgrims reached Plymouth?
a: An English ship carrying about 24 Angolan captives
A Spanish fleet claiming the Virginia coast
A group of free Black farmers bound for Plymouth
A colonial treaty ending the slave trade
questions.why: The overview introduces the White Lion and the first Black residents of what became the United States.

questions.q: Why did Virginia's elite pass laws restricting Black residents after the 1676 rebellion?
a: They feared another uprising of Black and white workers together
They wanted to raise money through new taxes
They were pressured by church leaders to do so
They hoped the laws would attract more settlers
questions.why: The first lesson says the elite crushed the rebellion but were frightened by its multiracial alliance.

questions.q: What did the 1667 law about Christian baptism establish?
a: Baptism did not make an enslaved person free
Only Christians were allowed to own land
Churches could buy an enslaved person's freedom
Children of enslaved parents were born free
questions.why: The first lesson says this law meant the church could not protect Black people from enslavement.

questions.q: What did the 1793 Fugitive Slave Act do?
a: Allowed escaped enslaved people to be seized in free states
Granted citizenship to free Black Americans
Banned slavery throughout the northern states
Required schools to teach Black history
questions.why: The second lesson says the act also made it illegal to help anyone who had escaped.

questions.q: What did Hurricane Katrina expose, according to the summary?
a: The government's systemic disregard for Black Americans
The strength of local emergency planning
The speed of New Orleans' recovery
The fairness of federal aid distribution
questions.why: The third lesson calls Katrina a humanitarian disaster that laid bare how the state neglected Black communities.
